name: Bimagrumab

lead: Bimagrumab is an antibody that blocks the activin receptors that limit muscle growth. In trials it increased lean mass and reduced fat, and Lilly is testing it with GLP-1 drugs to protect muscle during weight loss.
It is investigational only, given by infusion in trials, and not a product people can obtain legitimately.

paras: It occupies ActRIIA/ActRIIB, preventing myostatin, activins and GDF11 from signalling, which allows muscle growth and affects fat tissue.

No approval exists. Reported side effects include muscle spasms, diarrhoea and acne according to an unverified AI-generated summary, and strength or function gains were not demonstrated in older adults.

lead: Bimagrumab (BYM338, LY3985863) is an investigational fully human monoclonal antibody that blocks activin type II receptors (ActRIIA and ActRIIB), the receptors through which myostatin, activins and related signals restrain muscle growth. [1][2][3] It was developed by Novartis, and Eli Lilly acquired rights to it through its purchase of Versanis Bio in 2023, according to an AI-generated encyclopedia summary. [4]

It is not approved for any use. It has been trialled in sporadic inclusion body myositis, sarcopenia, recovery after hip fracture surgery, type 2 diabetes with obesity, and, more recently, obesity in combination with incretin drugs such as semaglutide and tirzepatide, where the goal is to lose fat while preserving muscle. [5][6][7][8][9]

A phase 2 trial in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity reported significant loss of body fat and gain of lean mass over 48 weeks. [6] Trials in sarcopenia and inclusion body myositis increased muscle mass, but the benefit for strength or function was not shown, according to the AI-generated summary. [4] Its interest in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles stems from the "gain muscle while losing fat" profile; no community discussion of it was available for this entry.
infobox: Activin type II receptor (ActRII) monoclonal antibody
Novartis; later Versanis Bio and Eli Lilly

paras: Bimagrumab was designed to prevent ligands such as myostatin, GDF11 and activins from binding ActRII. Preclinical work reported that it induces strong skeletal muscle hypertrophy and protects against atrophy, and that blocking both ActRIIA and ActRIIB is required for maximal muscle growth in mice. [10][11] A review notes that blocking the receptor has also been associated with effects on brown fat in preclinical models. [3]

A pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analysis of the drug (BYM338) has been published in a clinical pharmacology journal. [12] The AI-generated summary gives a half-life of about 19 days and intravenous administration, which has not been checked against the primary pharmacokinetic paper here. [4]

Obesity and diabetes: a phase 2 randomised trial (2021, JAMA Network Open) tested bimagrumab versus placebo for body fat mass in adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity, after prior studies suggested ActRII inhibition promotes loss of excess adipose tissue and improves insulin resistance. [6] According to the AI-generated summary, it reduced total fat mass by about 7.5 kg versus 0.2 kg with placebo over 48 weeks while increasing lean mass and lowering HbA1c. [4]

Combination with incretin drugs: a phase 2 trial published in Nature Medicine in 2026 tested bimagrumab with semaglutide, alone or combined, in obesity. [7] The AI-generated summary reports greater weight loss with the combination than with semaglutide alone and smaller lean-mass loss, but these figures have not been verified against the paper. [4] Further registered trials combine bimagrumab with tirzepatide, though one planned study in people with type 2 diabetes was withdrawn. [13][14] Reviews note that GLP-1-type drugs can cause loss of fat-free mass, up to 40 percent of weight lost in some analyses, motivating this approach. [15][16]

Sarcopenia: a 2020 randomised trial compared bimagrumab plus standard of care with standard of care alone in community-dwelling older adults with sarcopenia, and a 2017 phase 2 proof-of-concept study examined it in the same condition; a 2024 meta-analysis of randomised trials assessed effects on physical performance and body composition. [8][1][17] The AI-generated summary states that muscle mass rose without improved physical performance and that Novartis stopped the sarcopenia programme. [4]

Myositis and hip fracture: bimagrumab was tested in sporadic inclusion body myositis, including a phase 2b trial published in Lancet Neurology, and after hip fracture surgery in a phase 2 study. [18][19][20] The AI-generated summary says muscle volume rose without clear gains in strength or function in myositis. [4]

The AI-generated summary lists muscle spasms, diarrhoea and acne as common side effects, which should be treated as unverified here. [4] Phase 1 and 2 safety assessments across indications are reported in the trials above. [6][8]

Lilly lists bimagrumab among obesity pipeline assets, and registered studies include a phase 1 study with tirzepatide in healthy participants and a planned phase 2 study in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. [13][21][22] Reviews describe activin and myostatin inhibitors, including trevogrumab and garetosmab, as a category aimed at preserving lean mass during weight loss. [16]

timeline.event: Preclinical papers describe bimagrumab-type ActRII blockade as inducing strong muscle hypertrophy; trials begin in inclusion body myositis. [10][23]
Phase 2 proof-of-concept study in sarcopenia published. [17]
Phase 2 trial reports fat loss in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity. [6]
Eli Lilly acquires Versanis Bio, which held bimagrumab (per AI-generated summary). [4]
Phase 2 bimagrumab plus semaglutide trial published in Nature Medicine. [7]
